The target systems obey nonlinear partial integro-differential equations with local rhythmic behavior. A Galerkin projection shrinks the system onto a learned basis of spatial shapes. The team then learns the flow map of the projected ODEs directly. That skips costly step-by-step integration at run time. Tests on a neural field system beat a leading neural operator, they report.
arxiv-2603-18167: Cicoli and co-authors review axions in the meV mass range across theory, cosmology, astrophysics, and experiments. This range is well motivated and can appear in ultraviolet-complete models. MeV axions could act as dark matter or dark radiation with clear cosmic effects. Stars and supernovae give strong probes through efficient axion production. Search methods span helioscopes, haloscopes, quasiparticle systems, and large Cherenkov detectors, as set out at a 2025 Frascati workshop.
arxiv-2603-18267: Pharr and co-authors quantify resonant drive in resistive perturbed tokamak equilibria. Two common metrics, one for shielding current and one for penetrated field, had no known relation. With a resistive MHD inner layer in GPEC, the penetrated field scales as S to the minus two thirds. Both metrics pick closely similar dominant coupling modes in the same model. Resistive physics shifts that spectrum to lower mode numbers in a low-rotation ITER case.
arxiv-2603-18367: Lan and Meng steady highly nonlinear hybrid stochastic delay equations with bursts of feedback. Their controller acts in on-off bursts and reads the state only at set times. The system and the controller may switch modes out of step with each other. They bound how long the gaps between reads can be and how wide each burst must stay. Moment-based stability and its rate are proved, with more burst time tied to a faster rate.
arxiv-2603-18667: Tripathy, Mathur, and Padmanath search lattice QCD data for bound tetraquarks with two bottom quarks. They also test the bottom-strange channel. Runs use four ensembles with varied lattice spacing and two volumes to check size effects. A variational method gives finite-volume energies, then Lüscher analysis extracts scattering behavior. The doubly bottom channel shows strong evidence for a deeply bound state. The bottom-strange channel gives no firm sign of a bound state. The isoscalar channel is the focus throughout the study.
arxiv-2603-18867: Floater proves an identity that ties multiple integrals with Vandermonde polynomials to divided differences. The same identity can be read as an integral formula for divided differences. Vandermonde polynomials carry the classic product of pairwise variable gaps. During the proof, Floater shows that sums of pure partial derivatives of these polynomials vanish. Sums of mixed partial derivatives vanish as well. That side result may interest readers on its own. The identity gives analysts a new bridge between integration and finite difference calculus.
arxiv-2603-19467: Demirci and Mustamin use solar neutrino data from LUX-ZEPLIN to bound light new physics. The detector's low-energy electron recoil results are the sharpest of their kind. They study scattering shaped by light mediators of scalar, vector, and tensor type. A second class adds a new gauge force tied to lepton flavor counts. Best solar flux values feed the cross-section math for each case. New limits are set across the coupling and mass plane. The bounds beat prior lab and space limits in fresh zones.
arxiv-2603-19967: Pereira and co-authors test a lean method for teaching students to frame research problems in software engineering. Lean Research Inception aims to keep problems tied to real practice. Their case study covered 60 students and 7 faculty advisors at a Brazilian university. Students reported gains in reasoning, clarity, and putting problems in context. Communication gains were also reported by half the group. Advisors saw clearer, better structured problems in most cases. A large share of advisors said they would recommend the method.
arxiv-2603-20167: Brusaschi and co-authors train a quantum learning machine on bright classical light, then run it on true quantum states. Quantum measurements are noisy, so normal training needs many repeated shots. That demand strains time and gear on large datasets. Their twin beams come from stimulated emission and carry the training signal. Inference then targets unseen quantum inputs directly. Using biphoton states, the system witnessed two qubit entanglement at 93 percent accuracy. It also learned the Hamiltonian of the pair source at 96 percent fidelity.
arxiv-2603-20267: Gao and co-authors make tree of thought reasoning cheaper with a small plug and play predictor. Tree search explores many branches, but model based scoring of each branch costs a lot. Rigid heuristics are cheaper yet inflexible across tasks. Their DST predictor is a light supervised model that guides the search. It prunes in a context aware way, staying near greedy on easy steps. The beam widens only when the predictor senses uncertainty or complexity. Accuracy matched or beat strong baselines while compute fell by 26 to 75 percent.
arxiv-2603-20367: Guerra and co-authors run the first detailed test of atomic dark matter effects on stellar streams. Their simulation follows a Milky Way-mass galaxy with a small atomic dark matter share. This share, about 6%, can cool and form dense compact objects. Satellites grow denser centers and resist being torn apart by tides. Streams above a mass threshold form later than in standard models. Their stars also show shifted iron and magnesium patterns. The results may extend to other dark matter models with denser satellites.
arxiv-2603-20467: Zou and co-authors learn surrogate models for stochastic differential equations with a goal in mind. Cheap surrogates speed up simulation of costly systems. But standard loss functions give no error bounds for path based outputs. Mean first hitting times are one such output. The team derives a bound for these path-space observables. They use that bound as a new loss for learning the drift function. A Fréchet derivative formula makes the loss gradient tractable in practice.
arxiv-2603-20567: Joshi and Prodan examine quantum adiabatic algorithms for problems with many solutions. They point out a topological snag in such cases. Spectral branches must cross the gap above the ground state. That fact casts doubt on how the method should work. Yet with Max-Cut as a test case, they show the algorithms still find all solutions in one run. This skill, they argue, could shape future quantum variational methods.
arxiv-2603-20867: Javidnia argues that model features should not always be treated as single global directions. In some representation spaces, a meaning can stay coherent locally yet fail to join into one global feature. He introduces semantic sections, families of local feature forms that must agree as they move across contexts. He proves tree based spread always works, while cycles decide if a section can go global. He then builds a pipeline to find and certify sections. Tests on three small instruct models find real groups of globalizable and twisted sections.
arxiv-2603-20967: Ghosh and co-authors show that hard labels can mislead rotation invariant learning methods. In logistic regression, feedback can be soft labels, the true class chances, or hard labels sampled from them. With soft labels, a sparse target can be recovered exactly in a favorable setting. They prove rotation invariant methods, such as gradient descent on the logistic loss, incur excess risk tied to the full dimension. A simple method that splits each weight into a product of two parts does far better.
arxiv-2603-21267: Ammari proves regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities through optimal transport. He uses an anisotropic form of Caffarelli's contraction theorem. He also gives a full picture of when the Brascamp-Lieb constant stays finite and when Gaussian extremizers exist. Heat flow methods, plus new ideas for the added difficulties, identify all optimizers of the regularized inequalities. The regularized setting brings problems that the classic case does not have. He closes with applications of the results.
arxiv-2603-21467: Filipović and co-authors report a diffuse radio source nicknamed Anglerfish, found in the ASKAP EMU survey at 944 MHz. The emission overlaps an infrared source whose colors suggest an elliptical galaxy, plus a semi-variable star. They test three identities: a stellar mass-loss remnant, a galactic supernova remnant, and an Odd Radio Circle around the galaxy. The star link looks unlikely, and the size and brightness fit a supernova remnant poorly. They favor the Odd Radio Circle reading, pending more observations.
arxiv-2603-21567: Shportko studies the information cost of hiding messages inside language model output. A steganographic rewrite keeps the surface meaning of a cover text while smuggling in a payload. Shportko proves a lower bound using Kolmogorov complexity: the hidden text must carry at least the cover's complexity plus the payload's, up to a small term. So any real payload forces the output's complexity up. Since true complexity cannot be computed, he tests perplexity ratios as a practical detector on 300 samples.
arxiv-2603-21767: Wang and co-authors ask whether changing-look active galactic nuclei mark a special stage in black hole and galaxy growth. These nuclei flip their spectral type within about a decade. Prior work on broad-line cases placed them in mid-to-old stellar populations. The team extends the test to narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, thought to host young black holes. A large catalog search found just three changing-look cases among 884 objects. Spectra show the pattern still holds, with these cases at the young edge of that group.
arxiv-2603-21867: Borsukiewicz and co-authors design face patterns that fool recognition systems, to shield people from mass surveillance. Their Adversarial Camouflage searches a small pattern space built from color, shape, and angle. Winning patterns are placed on valid face regions and scored across recognition models. The search maximizes error, so the patterns transfer even to black-box systems. Tests degraded every leading model they tried in simulation. Early real-world trials with human wearers looked promising. The method is meant to be cheap for ordinary users to copy.
arxiv-2603-22167: Chen and co-authors study calibeating, a way to post-process forecasts online. The goal is to cut cumulative loss and match a benchmark based on informativeness. Earlier work treated one loss at a time with bespoke arguments. The team instead reduces calibeating to standard online learning tools. They show it is minimax-equivalent to regret minimization. That recovers the known log T rate for Brier and log losses and gives new rates for other losses. They extend the same link to multi-calibeating and the expert problem.
arxiv-2603-22267: Chang and co-authors present TiCo, a spoken dialogue model that obeys time limits. A user can ask for a 15 second reply, and TiCo aims to match that length. Most spoken models lack time awareness and miss such targets. The team builds TiCo-Bench to measure this skill. TiCo plants time markers as it speaks, so it can track elapsed time and adjust the rest. Training uses self-generation plus reinforcement learning, with no paired question-answer data. TiCo cuts duration error sharply against its backbone.
arxiv-2603-22667: Li and co-authors present a mapping method for unmanned surface vehicles that explore near-shore waters. Weak satellite signals and tight onboard compute make mapping hard. Fixed-size map grids also waste effort on empty open water. Their variable-resolution virtual map uses an adaptive quadtree. Far, sparse areas stay coarse, while rich areas get fine detail. A planner weighs pose and map uncertainty along each frontier. Tests in a marina simulator show safer behavior than rival methods. The method also uses onboard compute better in signal-poor settings.
arxiv-2603-23067: Alawode and co-authors present MLLM-HWSI, a language model for whole slide image understanding in pathology. Whole slide images hold diagnostic clues at many scales, from cells to the full slide. Most models compress a slide into one embedding, losing fine grounding. Their model aligns vision and language at four scales, likened to word, phrase, sentence, and paragraph. Two losses keep meaning coherent across scales. A light attention module packs cell data into compact tokens. The model sets new top scores on 13 benchmarks across six pathology tasks.
arxiv-2603-23467: Bakker surveys fresh progress in non-abelian Hodge theory for non-proper varieties. The mixed setting stretches the classic theory past compact spaces. He explains how the new tools build algebraic Shafarevich maps. Those maps then prove a form of the linear Shafarevich conjecture. The proof works for any algebraic variety. The survey ties the recent advances into one route from Hodge theory to the conjecture.
arxiv-2603-23867: Chen and co-authors test whether vision-language models keep reasoning well when image inputs shift. The prediction rules stay fixed, but the look of the inputs changes. Fine-tuned models score high on familiar data yet fail under such shifts, they find. Their method, VLC, splits the work in two. A vision model names the objects in the image. A circuit then applies the task rules exactly to those concepts. On three visual deduction tasks, VLC beats other approaches on out-of-distribution data.
arxiv-2603-24167: Draissi and co-authors present Walma, a system that spots memory corruption in WebAssembly modules. A single bug in Wasm linear memory can let a module attack its host, or a host tamper with a module. Walma renders memory snapshots as grayscale images. A convolutional network then classifies them, reading structure that simple statistics miss. Hiding corruption from Walma takes overwriting hundreds of kilobytes or more, they find. Across 53 test binaries, attestation costs stay between 1.07 and 1.69 times the base cost.
arxiv-2603-24367: Saroj and Panigrahi study how an alumina nanofluid droplet dries on a heated hydrophobic glass surface. Evaporation stays mostly in pinned contact line mode, and droplet height and contact angle fall in a straight line over time. They define a parameter that sorts the deposit patterns. Low heat gives rare polygonal network patterns at the rim. More heat gives a classic coffee ring, and high heat gives dual rings with central deposits.
arxiv-2603-24567: Chowdhury and co-authors propose a trust region method for constrained Bayesian optimisation in high-dimensional problems. Such problems are hard: costly evaluations, no gradients, and complex feasible regions. Their method converts constraints into a penalty term, giving one objective to model with a surrogate. A trust region limits the search near the current best point, which aids stability in high dimensions. Expected improvement picks each new evaluation point. On test problems, it finds high-quality feasible solutions with fewer evaluations than top rivals.
arxiv-2603-24667: Altavista and co-authors construct junctions where several ten-dimensional string theories meet at a nine-dimensional branch point. Such junctions give a dynamical realisation of cobordisms between string theories, as the Cobordism Conjecture predicts. The construction generalises recent work on interpolations between IIA and IIB domain walls, with a worldsheet description. Extra degrees of freedom stay gapped except at the branch point, where the gap closes and branching begins. Examples join heterotic, type 0, and type II theories and their orientifolds, including chiral theories whose fields flow between branches.
arxiv-2603-24967: Taparia and co-authors split the uncertainty of a large language model into three parts. One part comes from vague prompts. A second comes from gaps in what the model knows. The third comes from random choices made while it writes. Their tests show which part dominates can change with model size and task. Knowing the source helps teams audit reliability, spot likely false answers, and fix the right weakness instead of chasing one score.
arxiv-2603-25067: Ibnath, Rezvani, and Wong watch service quality in running programs without asking the programs to report it. Managers need tail latency and throughput as feedback, but kernels and hardware counters cannot see those numbers. Their library, eBeeMetrics, infers them from events that eBPF can observe, like system calls. It can stand in for direct reporting or add a second view of server behavior. Across latency-sensitive workloads, its estimates track measured throughput and delay closely. The tool is open source, so others can adopt it.
arxiv-2603-25367: Yamamoto pins down the 2-adic piece of a special automorphic representation of GL3. The representation, built by van Geemen and Top, is not self-dual. He shows its local part at 2 is parabolically induced from a GL2 block and a line. The character in play is unramified with a set value at 2. The GL2 piece is supercuspidal, and he writes it as compact induction with an explicit inner type. Computer checks of Hecke eigenvalues drive the proof. A Galois-side payoff follows.
arxiv-2603-25467: Eltahir and co-authors reframe video anomaly spotting as propose, ground, then track. Vision-language models can name odd events freely, but raw use swings between misses and false alarms. GridVAD lets the model propose suspects over striped frame grids. A self-consistency pass keeps only proposals that recur across samples. Grounding DINO boxes each survivor, and SAM2 grows it into a mask across the event. On UCSD Ped2 the pixel score tops all rivals, even a partly tuned one. The call budget stays fixed per clip.
arxiv-2603-25767: Zhou and co-authors argue that audio pre-training needs stronger labels, not just new objectives. Current methods rely on weak, noisy labels with limited scale. The authors build a pipeline that uses a high-fidelity captioner to write top-quality captions. They also create a Unified Tag System spanning speech, music, and everyday sounds. With this data, they compare several pre-training objectives. Their results suggest that data quality and coverage drive most of the gains. The choice of objective mainly shapes which downstream tasks do best.
arxiv-2603-25867: Lu and co-authors present a model that removes surgical smoke from endoscopic video. Smoke from cautery tools clouds the view in minimally invasive surgery. Their transformer model predicts both a clean image and a smoke map. Paired training data is scarce, so they built a pipeline that blends fake smoke into real images. It produced over 80,000 training pairs. They also gathered 5,817 real pairs from a da Vinci surgical system. The model beat prior dehazing methods on reconstruction, they report. Tests also probe effects on depth and tool segmentation.
arxiv-2603-26367: Raviv and Shlezinger introduce WiMamba, a wireless foundation model built for scale. Transformer-based wireless models cost grows with the square of input size, which limits real use. WiMamba swaps attention for selective state-space blocks from the Mamba design, giving linear-time sequence work. A self-supervised training scheme built for radio channels teaches it transferable channel traits. Across four downstream tasks, WiMamba matches or beats transformer rivals. It also cuts delay and memory use by large margins.
arxiv-2603-26567: Alebachew and co-authors introduce StackRepoQA, a benchmark for answering questions about whole code repositories. Most tests use single functions or files, while real program understanding spans many files. The dataset holds 1,318 real developer questions with accepted answers from 134 open Java projects. They test Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o in direct and agentic setups, plus retrieval methods that use file search and dependency graphs. Baseline accuracy is modest, structure helps, and high scores often come from copying Stack Overflow text.
arxiv-2603-26667: Sun and co-authors propose M-RAG, a semantic key-value index layer for retrieval-augmented generation under a token budget. Most pipelines use the same text chunks for lookup and for evidence, though the two jobs pull apart. Small chunks split key facts, while large ones waste context on noise. M-RAG pulls meta-markers from whole documents, each holding a search key, a value payload, and provenance links. Lookup runs on the compact keys, and matched values fill the prompt in a position-aware order.
arxiv-2603-26867: Choi and co-authors revisit the domain wall problem of the DFSZ axion model. They show that the global structure of the symmetry group shapes the problem itself. In some quark flavor models, a non-invertible chiral symmetry keeps the domain walls stable. Small instantons can break that symmetry and resolve the problem. The authors also sketch gravitational wave signals from wall collapse. The work stresses that global structure matters in realistic particle models.
arxiv-2603-26967: Pattanayak and co-authors derive exact laws for torque-driven active Brownian particles in a harmonic trap. Chirality, self-propulsion, and confinement together shape the position spread over time. Their Laplace transform method solves the Fokker-Planck equation in 2D and in 3D. Closed forms give moments up to fourth order, including the excess kurtosis. In 2D, kurtosis oscillates and crosses regimes as stiffness grows. In 3D, it stays negative, marking band-like position patterns. The results give clear signatures of confined chiral motion.
arxiv-2603-27267: Padhan and co-authors examine how rotation shifts chemical freeze-out in heavy-ion collisions. Within the hadron resonance gas model, they extend standard freeze-out criteria to include global rotation. The criteria are fixed energy per particle and scaled entropy density. Rotation moves the freeze-out curve toward lower temperatures. Electric charge and strangeness chemical potentials gain their first such study in this model. Hadron yield ratios respond clearly to the rotation strength. Cumulant ratios of conserved charges barely move by contrast.
arxiv-2603-27467: Patel shrinks the memory cache that language models keep while writing. His TurboAngle method stores cache entries as angles. A random rotation spreads value pairs near-uniformly on a circle. Each layer can use its own codebook sizes. Key layers get more bits than the rest. Tests span seven models from one to seven billion parameters. Four models show no quality loss at all. Six of seven stay near-lossless. Total cost lands at 6.56 bits per element on Mistral-7B.
arxiv-2603-27667: Xie and co-authors argue audio models fail first at hearing, not reasoning. EvA keeps acoustic evidence intact before any reasoning begins. Two paths merge sound cues without crushing time detail. A new training set backs the design. It holds about 54,000 ordered captions. It also holds 500,000 evidence-based question pairs. EvA tops open-source perception scores on three benchmarks. Human raters praise its fine caption detail.
arxiv-2603-27867: Domoradzki and co-authors reflect on ninety years of the Scottish Book. The book of problems grew in a Lwów café circle. New math fields trace roots to its pages. Junior scholars drew stimulation from its open questions. A decade of progress since the last review is summed. Solved problems get fresh status notes. Kindred problem collections are surveyed as well. The piece honors a living problem tradition.
arxiv-2603-28567: Ares, Das, and Kundu study symmetry-resolved entanglement entropy in a driven compact boson field theory. They track how Rényi entropies for each charge sector move toward or away from equal shares. A Virasoro subalgebra brings in a free label, k, that can control the break from equipartition. They argue that the effect comes from coupling between low and high frequency modes. The same mechanism may hold beyond the free boson case. They also study boundary state dynamics under non-unitary evolution, linked to post-selected weak measurements.
arxiv-2603-28967: Dean and co-authors work toward a formalism for pion-pion scattering from staggered lattice QCD. The Lüscher method links finite volume energy levels to scattering amplitudes. Rooted staggered fermions break unitarity as a lattice artifact, and taste splitting gives several pion types. Those traits limit the Lüscher method at nonzero lattice spacing. The team pursues two routes. One uses rooted staggered chiral perturbation theory to compute one loop amplitudes and check the quantization condition. The other generalizes the formalism to include taste splitting.
arxiv-2603-29067: Zhao and co-authors ask what gains remain after localization is strengthened in repository level repair. They study three RAG based repair systems on SWE-bench Lite. Oracle localization improves all three, yet oracle success still stays below 50 percent. Extra candidate diversity helps inside sampled patch pools, but that headroom saturates quickly. Most added context beats matched controls under interfaces. A common wrapper check gives different responses per system. Prompt level fusion leaves a large residual frontier: the best probe adds only six solved cases beyond the union.
arxiv-2603-29167: Ma and co-authors present JDCNet, a way to train X-ray models with CT help. CT scans guide training, but deployment uses X-rays alone. That keeps cost and speed equal to a plain X-ray baseline. The CT teacher gives extra targets only when its confidence passes a set threshold. On 510 paired patients, two JDCNet variants beat the supervised baseline. Several rival distillation methods failed the same transfer gate. The authors warn that one cohort bounds the evidence.
arxiv-2603-29667: Zhang and co-authors simulate flow through and around a round array of cylinders. The array has six-fold symmetry, and patch density varies across six designs. They combine direct simulations with global stability analysis. The focus is where vortex shedding begins. Three regimes appear as density grows. At low density, cylinders act nearly alone and wakes stay steady. At mid density, the onset point shifts like flow in a porous medium. At high density, the array behaves like one solid cylinder.
arxiv-2604-00567: Bergach removes twiddle-factor singularities from the radix-2 FFT butterfly. The fused multiply-add runs the butterfly in 6 operations, the minimum. The Linzer-Feig factorisation precomputes a cotangent ratio, which blows up when the twiddle factor equals 1 and sine hits zero. Clamping sine to epsilon harms precision. A cosine-outside alternative avoids that blow-up but creates one at a quarter turn. Bergach's dual-select picks, each time, whichever factorisation keeps the ratio at most 1 in size. That ends all singularities, with no clamping.
arxiv-2604-00767: Ray and colleagues propose ActivityNarrated, an open-ended narrative approach to wearable activity recognition that replaces fixed-window, closed-set labels with dense sensor captions. Their ActNarrator system turns steady motion-sensor signals into reusable motion tokens, then uses a small frozen language model to write open-vocabulary activity captions. It beats leading activity-recognition models on later classification tests and supports question answering over long spans.
arxiv-2604-00867: Fehrentz and colleagues equip surgical agents with an explicit 4D representation built from single-camera keyhole-surgery video, grounding language reasoning in time and 3D space. Point tracking, depth, and segmentation models combine into a coherent model with consistent tool and tissue meanings. A language model that handles images and text then acts as an agent on its tools without fine-tuning. Tested on 134 clinically relevant questions, the combination markedly improves space-and-time understanding and enables 4D grounding.
arxiv-2604-00967: Van Berkel and Lyon build a modular framework for deontic STIT logic, the study of multi-agent choice-making, covering the many readings of the principle that ought implies can. They discuss, compare, and formalize ten readings, supply sound and complete sequent-style calculi for the STIT logics holding each principle, and analyze how the readings relate logically. They also propose an endorsement principle stating which readings commit one to others.
arxiv-2604-01167: Deb and colleagues propose AdaLoRA-QAT, a two-stage tuning setup pairing low-rank encoder changes with quantization-aware training for chest X-ray segmentation. Adaptive rank picks make tuning leaner, while mixed-precision quantization keeps shape fidelity crucial for reliability. Across chest X-ray sets it achieves 95.6% Dice, matching full-precision SAM tuning while cutting weights 17-fold and shrinking the model more than twofold. A Wilcoxon signed-rank test confirms quantization does not degrade segmentation accuracy, showing it holds accuracy, efficiency and trustworthiness in balance for models.
arxiv-2604-01367: Koehler and Leung study approximating the permanent of a matrix with entries biased away from zero, motivated by linear optics and boson sampling. Barvinok's interpolation method enables efficient approximation given a large zero-free region for the permanent. For complex Gaussian entries, all zeros of the random polynomial lie within a disk of radius order n to the power minus one-third. This yields an approximation algorithm when the bias is of the same order. They also show most zeros have magnitude order n to the power minus one-half.
arxiv-2604-01667: Dong and colleagues propose a multi-stage dynamic fusion strategy for sample-adaptive brain network analysis. Current fusion methods in brain networks, focusing on structural and functional connectivity, are static: they feed different samples into the same model with identical computation. Unlike static fusion methods, they design different mixture-of-experts for uni- and multi-modal representations where modules change as input samples change during inference. To prevent training collapse, they divide the method into 3 stages: first training uni-modal encoders, then pretraining single experts before finetuning the whole model.
arxiv-2604-02067: Mettasch counts rational points of bounded height on a quadric over a function field using the circle method. Viewing points as morphisms of fixed degree, the formulas depend on the parity of the degree and the determinant of the defining quadratic form, with secondary terms in some cases. The work extends a classical counting machine to function fields, giving precise totals where only rough estimates might be expected.
arxiv-2604-02167: Samanta, Hazra and Pradhan derive exact density correlations for mass transport on lattices with hopping that favors some directions and mirrors across axes. Adding center of mass conservation changes the power law: conserved in all directions, correlations decay faster and the system shows extreme uniformity, with long wavelength fluctuations suppressed. Conserved along only some directions, the slower decay returns. A charge analogy explains the shift, with higher charge patterns giving the faster law.
arxiv-2604-02267: Ekinci and colleagues determine exact S-packing chromatic numbers for paths and cycles. For a non decreasing sequence of positive integers, an S-packing coloring requires same color vertices to sit farther apart than the color index allows. They pin the exact number for every path under sequences meeting a per entry condition, naming critical and vertex critical paths. They extend earlier cycle results to a full account of critical and vertex critical cycles for sequences meeting two conditions.
arxiv-2604-03267: Vazquez-Garcia and colleagues build a smart camera platform that segments and characterizes jet flames on the device for industrial fire safety. Running an optimized UNet model on a system-on-chip FPGA, the platform processes video at the edge with low latency instead of shipping it elsewhere. Shrinking the model from 7.5 million to 59,095 parameters, the system reaches 30 frames per second without losing accuracy.
arxiv-2604-03367: Chakraborty, Souslov, and Castelnovo study two one-way coupled copies of Ising gauge theory that keep a local twofold symmetry. Their combined Wilson loop scales linearly, with a pair binding length set by coupling strength. Strong interactions drive single excitations along self-avoiding trails on a critical percolation cluster, tuning noise spectra and trapping quasiparticles into long-lived metastable states.
arxiv-2604-03667: Daniele Materia and colleagues worked on guessing which object a person wearing a camera will handle next. Their method marks candidate objects in the view and follows the wearer's recent eye movements to read intent, sampling frames more densely just before contact. On the HD-EPIC egocentric collection, the approach beat previous methods and worked across different vision-language models.
arxiv-2604-03767: Taichi Uyama and colleagues found a low-mass companion, HIP 53005 C, about 62 astronomical units from the young star HIP 53005. The find used Subaru and Keck images plus Hipparcos-Gaia motion data. Its colors and spectrum place it near the line between M and L dwarfs and near the hydrogen-burning limit, around 80 Jupiter masses. Yet orbit fits favor a far heavier dynamical mass near 185 Jupiter masses, a clash a hidden close companion or a low-mass binary might explain.
arxiv-2604-04167: Veli Shahmurov and Rishad Shahmurov studied the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes system with an added nonlocal damping term. They identified a sharp Fourier-symbol test sorting weak convolution tweaks from truly smoothing nonlocal effects. In this hyperdissipative class they proved the exact energy identity, global weak solvability for every alpha above 1, and local strong solutions for smooth data. The Lions exponent of 5 over 4 remains the critical growth threshold, above which every solution is global.
arxiv-2604-04867: Chaussidon and colleagues map the outward velocity of matter by joining microwave sky maps with galaxy surveys. Using Atacama Cosmology Telescope and DESI data, they map speeds for luminous red galaxies, emission-line galaxies, and quasars. They model foreground noise with care and find it barely affects the main results. The velocity-galaxy signal appears at 17.0 sigma for red galaxies, with first sightings for the other two classes, plus a first velocity-velocity sighting.
arxiv-2604-05067: Aman, Asaduzzaman, and Wang introduce Typify, a static analysis engine for precise Python type inference. Python's dynamic type system offers freedom, yet poses problems for static analysis in code with few or no type marks. Existing approaches depend on notes or on deep learning models needing large training corpora and heavy compute, which limits scale and clarity. Typify infers precise, apt type information without stats learning or large data. It joins symbolic checks with fixpoint analysis and a context lookup system to ground results in how code is used.
arxiv-2604-05167: Shen and three colleagues frame reserve design, choosing the shape to cut dispatch cost under a cover target. Shaping the cover constraint into a radius turns the problem into a goal, with KKT information giving task slopes. A split mixes a quantile gauge with even tuning, yielding cover. It is tested on the IEEE system with transfer constraints. The learned shape cuts dispatch cost by about 4.8 percent while keeping cover above target.
arxiv-2604-05267: Do, Le, and Tran ask whether domain-specific experts exist in mixture-of-experts language models. Across ten advanced models from 3.8B to 120B parameters, they find empirical evidence for domain-specific experts. They propose Domain Steering Mixture of Experts, a training-free framework with zero additional inference cost that outperforms well-trained models and supervised fine-tuning baselines. On four open-source models across target and non-target domains, it shows strong performance and robust generalization without added inference cost or retraining.
arxiv-2604-05567: Baron-Prada and three colleagues develop containment rules for scaled graphs inside multiplier-defined circular and conic regions. For circles, soft and hard containment coincide when the multiplier is positive-negative, letting soft computations certify hard stability. Tests on systems up to 300 states save 15 to 44 percent of compute, and conic regions bound nonsymmetric operators more tightly than circles.
arxiv-2604-05767: Goldshmidt and three colleagues advance collision anticipation with BADAS-2.0, built on fine-tuned V-JEPA2 over dashcam data. A 10-group long-tail benchmark grows labeled video from 40k to 178,500 clips. Distillation yields compact edge models 7 to 12 times faster at near-parity accuracy. Heatmaps plus a vision-language reasoner explain predictions in real time.
arxiv-2604-05867: Pinto and Ribeiro run the Blahut-Arimoto algorithm on GPU chips to bound binary deletion channel capacity, where bits vanish at random. Their fast code caps capacity at about 0.36 times one minus the loss rate once loss passes about two thirds. The result gives a sharp limit for codes over lossy links.
arxiv-2604-06567: Pallotta and five colleagues present a PMP-based Earth-system setup. Deep-learning models promise fast partners for older models. Their setup tests these models with PCMDI tests. It rates ACE2 and NeuralGCM on climate, shifts, monsoons, and rain against field and CMIP-class benchmarks. Judging these models with traditional tools extends assessment beyond skill toward longer uses. Results show strengths in large-scale fields and shift modes, alongside challenges in rain, tropical shifts, and stability for some versions. This evaluation builds trust, guides development, and clarifies their fit.
arxiv-2604-06767: Brett studies the Voronoi tessellation of a converged language model's representation space. Using float32 margin recomputation to clear bfloat16 artifacts, he confirms a linear scaling law for the expressibility gap with an R-squared near one, the strongest confirmation to date. A mid-layer ambiguity zone appears where margin geometry runs against cross-entropy before aligning at the final layer. Margin refinement procedures then reshape the tessellation without retraining: Fisher-based refinement holds damage steady near 5,300 positions while lifting median margins by 28 percent, though gains cluster in frequent structural tokens.
arxiv-2604-06867: Ishant and four colleagues compare two frustrated metallic compounds with muon-spin probes. HoCdCu4 orders fully below its transition, while HoInCu4 shows strong frustration instead. In HoInCu4 only 30 percent of holmium moments join static order below transition, while 70 percent keep dynamic correlations down to three tenths of a kelvin, resembling quantum spin-liquid behavior. Relaxation rates also hint at quantum critical fluctuations near transition, marking HoInCu4 as a proximate quantum spin liquid, a first for frustrated metals, backed by neutron results.
arxiv-2604-07067: Škrjanec and three colleagues test whether two tongue language models copy how two tongue people read shared word forms. People read true friends, words alike in form and sense, a bit faster, while false friends, words alike in form but not sense, slow them or do nothing. The team trained Dutch English models under four ways of sharing word codes, then probed them with word sets from human reading tests. Only when true friends alone shared codes did the human pattern show up.
arxiv-2604-07167: Hugenroth, Danry, and Maes present Critical Inker, a writing tool that scaffolds critical thought while a language model helps draft text. As auto writing spreads, users risk offloading thought to the machine and losing sharpness. Critical Inker fights this with two aids: a Socratic chat bot that asks questions to expose and fix logic slips, and visual marks that flag logic slips with no chat. The team reports strong argument overlap with human tags and strong validity accuracy, plus early feedback from a small pilot study.
arxiv-2604-07267: Allison, Maciazek, and Stephenson develop theory for scalable Gaussian process regression with nearest neighbors. Full Gaussian process regression costs cubic time in training size, limiting massive datasets, so practitioners predict from each test point's nearest neighbors, as in NNGP and GPnn methods. Under mild regularity assumptions, the authors derive sure pointwise limits for mean squared error, calibration, and negative log-likelihood. They study L2 risk, prove universal consistency, and show risk attains Stone's minimax rate, plus uniform convergence of mean squared error over compact hyperparameter sets with derivatives vanishing asymptotically.
arxiv-2604-07367: Whyte and five colleagues build a general economic-viability framework for fusion plants, modeled on the Lawson criterion for energy gain. The model uses steady timing plus engineering and cost parameters scaled to the energy capture surface. Its economic gain criteria thus ignore absolute plant power and stay neutral across fusion technologies. Deriving the economic gain factor gives curved equations governed by ten scaled design parameters, from power density and component lifetime to energy price and efficiency. Sweeping those parameters widely reveals trade-offs that can aid viable fusion.
arxiv-2604-07467: Osakuade and King show that discrete speech units, the quantized tokens used to model speech alongside text, capture lexical tone poorly. Self-supervised speech representations themselves do encode tone in Mandarin and Yorùbá, yet quantization prioritizes phonetic structure over suprasegmental detail. The gap persists across quantization methods, not just the common K-means approach. A two-stage fix helps: cluster once for phonetic content, then cluster the residual again, which encodes tone far better, pointing toward tone-aware speech representations.
arxiv-2604-07567: Palaisti builds a data likelihood for moving aggregate auto copula models of state rating moves with changing risk. An annual count picks a chance transform interval, not a single latent point, so it sums over the full sequence of count bands. A guided stepwise Monte Carlo build folds the steady edge fix into this summing. In Fitch, Moody's, and S&P ratings from 1963 to 2025, MAGMAR beats plain MAG under a static margin, but under a dynamic margin tests favor plain MAG.
arxiv-2604-07667: Wang and 11 colleagues introduce Conformal Social Choice, a layer turning debate outputs into act-versus-escalate decisions. When agents converge on a wrong answer via reinforcement, consensus stopping commits that error to action. Spoken probabilities are pooled and calibrated with conformal prediction, yielding coverage: at any pre-set round, the correct answer is covered with probability at least 1 minus alpha. A policy maps singletons to action and larger sets to humans. At the last round, 81.9 percent of wrong cases are flagged at alpha equals 0.05.
arxiv-2604-07767: Li and five colleagues give phones more control in edge-cloud automation instead of leaving them as passive executors. Their AdecPilot system pairs a cloud designer that sketches abstract milestones with an on-device team that plans tactics and corrects itself. A stopping protocol halts the job cleanly and blocks hallucinations after completion. Task success rises 21.7 percent against EcoAgent, while cloud token use falls about 38 percent against EcoAgent and latency drops about 89 percent against CORE.
arxiv-2604-07867: Sagawa builds a stochastic thermodynamics framework for autoregressive sequence models, from transformers and recurrent networks to Kalman filters, state-space models, and Mamba. Such models sample each output from a fixed summary of the past, yielding truly non-Markovian observed runs. It introduces entropy production, which can be estimated from sampled runs without blowup despite that memory. A proof-of-concept test on trained GPT-2 finds token-level entropy output ruled by a grammar quirk, while sentence-level pattern tells another story.
arxiv-2604-08267: Ye factors the Ghilardi-Zawadowski sheaf view of finitely generated free Heyting systems into profinite limits. He then places their dual category inside a sheaf topos as a full subcategory of that topos. That dual category is infinitary, broad, and regular, with completion exactly that sheaf topos, the K-topos. Uniform interpolation traits extend to all such algebras, from the K-topos's internal logic.
arxiv-2604-08467: Patti and seven colleagues speed up tensor network simulations of noisy quantum systems by fixing three bottlenecks in batched trajectory sampling. Unified path variation, non degenerate sampling, and a flexible contraction setup lift data collection to over 100 million times the rate of standard trajectory methods. The same tools also give more than a thousandfold speedup for broader quantum simulations, with special strength for non proportional sampling.
arxiv-2604-08567: Yang and seven colleagues study language model agents that must serve several users at once, not one main user. They formalize multi user interaction as a multi principal decision problem and build a unified protocol with three stress tests for instruction following, privacy, and coordination. Frontier models often fail to hold stable priorities under conflicting goals, leak more privacy over long chats, and stall when coordination needs repeated information gathering.
arxiv-2604-08667: Balkin and six colleagues build a unified two to three setup for production of single particle states in forward proton motion for the future Electron-Ion Collider. It covers spin zero and vector mesons, axion like particles, and dark photon carriers. Its model based rates fit photo and production data and admit steady polish. Benchmarks against matching photon estimate accounts agree closely at near real photon energy, while finite energy links matter for fine grained measures.
arxiv-2604-08767: Dmitrii Stoliarov and seventeen colleagues show a high power O-band soliton microcomb for short reach data center links. It combines an 834 gigahertz self locked silicon nitride microcomb spanning 1050 to 1650 nanometres with a bismuth doped fiber amp. The system gives over 0 dBm per carrier for 21 O-band lines over 100 nanometres with low noise. A 25 km coherent test reaches 7.23 terabits per second total throughput, a usable route to multi terabit links.
arxiv-2604-08867: Kang, Fang, and Li build AudioGuard, a unified guardrail for audio safety across diverse threat models. Audio risks go beyond unsafe text spoken aloud, spanning harmful sound events, speaker traits like child voices, impersonation and voice cloning, and risky voice content combinations. Large scale red teaming uncovers system vulnerabilities and yields a policy grounded risk taxonomy plus AudioSafetyBench, the first benchmark for audio safety built on policy. AudioGuard pairs SoundGuard for waveform level detection with ContentGuard for semantic protection, beating strong audio language model baselines at lower latency.
arxiv-2604-09467: Greenstreet and six colleagues refine multi-stage trials that test several treatments at once and drop the weakest at each interim check. Their design also halts the whole trial early when one treatment proves clearly superior, cutting both the expected number of participants and the maximum enrollment funding must cover. An atrial fibrillation example shows it beating standard drop-the-loser designs on expected size.
arxiv-2604-09867: Taylor constructs a stepwise coherator, a model for endless groupoids with a base round set, using sharing series of monads. The setup supports a stepwise strategy for the broad Homotopy claim, moving model structure from n-groupoids to (n+1)-groupoids. Taylor gives a needed and enough condition for the transfer to succeed, and shows that if transfers complete in turn, the broad Homotopy claim holds.
arxiv-2604-10467: Adak caps how many edges a crown free linear hypergraph can hold. A linear hypergraph lets each vertex pair share at most one edge. His k-crown joins one base edge to k separate edges, each meeting the base once. The new cap beats a recent Zhang, Broersma, and Wang bound for all ranks from four up. Small cases match short linear paths and get their own direct treatment.
arxiv-2604-10867: Barkan, Heuts, and Shi compare routes into homotopy theory at chromatic height n: T(n)-homology versus v_n-periodic groups. Building on Bousfield's observation that the two differ greatly, their tool is parametric T(n)-equivalence, a map inducing an equivalence on local systems valued in T(n)-local spectra. Results are sharpest for infinite loop spaces, including a T(n)-local Kuhn result on Morava K-theory of the Whitehead tower. They give the L_n^f-localization of Omega-infinity E with vanishing L_{n-1}^f.
arxiv-2604-11167: Inoue and three colleagues test whether a torsion-bar detector can sense Yukawa-style departures from Newtonian gravity. Two rotating mass systems cancel the leading Newtonian torque, leaving a residual that maps to a strain signal below one hertz. Sensitivity peaks near eight meters, reaching a coupling strength of 0.000024 at that range, limited by imperfect cancellation and source-mass geometry rather than statistical noise.
arxiv-2604-11367: Santos and eight colleagues calculate how strain-induced curvature reshapes monolayer graphene. Curvature under a set strain constraint stabilizes the sheet. As curvature grows, Van Hove peaks in the electron density of states approach the Fermi energy, with flat and linear bands coexisting near that level, a promising mix for heat-to-power uses. The sheet stays dynamically stable across the studied strains. The flexural acoustic mode shifts from quadratic to linear form, boosting phonon scattering and lowering lattice heat flow, which strain can thus tune.
arxiv-2604-11467: Labarta and four colleagues make explanations actionable with activation steering. Their web tool combines sparse-autoencoder scores with steering for instance-level concept analysis in vision models. In expert interviews with eight experts doing debugging tasks on CLIP, steering shifted work from inspection to testing ideas by intervening for all eight. Most trusted observed responses over explanation appeal. The tool lets users test ideas by intervening, not just by looking. Users favored suppression and flagged ripple effects and limited generalization of instance fixes.
arxiv-2604-11867: Sadasivan reports a three-arc negative result on teaching small language models dispositions like self-verification and uncertainty acknowledgment. An internal draft claimed large gains, but a second check falsified them: the HumanEval gain was a truncation artifact flipping to minus 8.0 points at longer outputs, and the other gain vanished under fair scoring. Across model families, attention-head tempering, and a frozen-base sidecar, no method shifted judge-measured disposition without harming content or collapsing into mimicry. One Gemma model, too, asserts at 91 percent whether it is right or not.
arxiv-2604-12467: P. Lassègues and 31 colleagues report the first measurements of high excited states in francium atoms. They measure absolute energies and radiative lifetimes of the 9p and 10p levels. The work uses collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy on a beam of francium-221 atoms. No experimental data had existed for francium p-states above level eight. Results test relativistic coupled-cluster theory for the heaviest alkali metal. Lifetimes and relative energies agree well, despite a global offset in absolute energies.
arxiv-2604-12967: Sohyun An and four colleagues train search agents without gold answers. Gold supervision scales poorly, yet most methods depend on it. Cycle Consistent Search treats a good trajectory as a lossless encoding of question intent. High-quality trajectories preserve enough information to rebuild the original question. Naive cycle goals leak through lexical cues, so bottlenecks block that shortcut. Excluding the final response and masking named entities force reliance on retrieved observations. Tests match supervised baselines and beat prior gold free methods.
arxiv-2604-13267: Saha and ten colleagues report the first direct detection of ionizing photons from faint early galaxies, using deep ultraviolet imaging from AstroSat and Hubble. The photons emerge from stacked Lyman-alpha emitters at redshift 5.9 to 6.0 in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, implying greater transparency of interstellar and intergalactic media than models predict. The stacked spectrum shows a hard slope and an escape fraction near 0.8. Very blue continua, young ages, and low metallicities point to hot massive stars powering reionization, plus evidence that helium reionization had begun.
arxiv-2604-13467: Raphael Grondin proves that a classic entropy-rate theorem survives a flexible way of cutting data into blocks. As long as the block count grows more slowly than the data itself, the average surprise per block still settles on the entropy rate. The result also withstands small changes to the blocks, and Grondin shows the slow-growth condition cannot be loosened, by building a counterexample.
arxiv-2604-13967: Yan and Li study a power function with a Niho exponent, a family prized in sequence design, coding theory, and cryptography. By analyzing certain polynomials over a finite field, they determine the function's differential spectrum. The result shows the function is locally differentially 4-uniform, filling a gap in the known spectra for Niho-exponent power functions.
arxiv-2604-14267: Wang and six colleagues improve search agents with Contribution-Weighted GRPO, which folds process supervision into group relative policy optimization. Rather than optimizing process rewards outright, an LLM judge scores retrieval utility and reasoning correctness each round, and those per-round scores rescale outcome-based advantages along the trajectory. The approach gives fine-grained credit without sacrificing optimization stability, beating standard GRPO by about 5 percent on Qwen3-8B and about 6 percent on Qwen3-1.7B. Winning trajectories show contributions bunched in specific rounds, a clue for future search agent design.
arxiv-2604-14367: Coskun and Chitra develop a route to the many-body density of states for isolated, interacting quantum systems from generalized coherent states and Simon-Lieb bounds on the partition function. The framework bounds ground-state energy in each sector and supports microcanonical observables across the spectrum. Tests on the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model recover quantum phase transitions and excited-state transitions across spin sectors. On a ferromagnetic Ising chain under a transverse field with power-law interactions, the top spin sector's density of states matches the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick pattern.
arxiv-2604-14767: Kadosawa, Nakamura, Ohta, and Nishimoto map ground-state magnetism in an easy-axis spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on a triangular lattice. They track sublattice moments as anisotropy grows. At the isotropic point the positive moment is 0.217. In the easy-axis regime the moments stay near a Y-like two-m, minus-m, minus-m pattern, reaching 0.419 positive and 0.209 negative at huge anisotropy. The Y state beats the up-down-down state at zero field, so fluctuations preserve nontrivial order rather than saturated Ising order.
arxiv-2604-14967: Wang and seven others propose UniDoc-RL, a unified reinforcement learning framework for visual retrieval-augmented generation. Existing visual RAG systems use generic retrieval signals that miss fine visual semantics needed for complex reasoning. Their agent jointly performs retrieval, reranking, active perception, and reasoning, refining evidence from coarse search to fine selection and region cropping. A dense multi-reward scheme guides each action, and group relative policy optimization aligns behavior without a value network. Tests on three benchmarks show gains over baselines, up to 17.7 percent over prior RL-based methods.
arxiv-2604-15467: Gatza and Huang build a part-based reduced-order modeling scheme for large rocket engines, where full high-fidelity runs stay out of reach. Each part, injectors, combustor, and nozzle, gets its own reduced model trained on small-domain runs with enforced system-level responses, then the parts couple into full-system runs. On a seven-injector combustor with self-excited dynamics, predictions track spectra and field features well.
arxiv-2604-15667: Yu, writing for the sPHENIX Collaboration, reports open-charm baryon-to-meson ratios in proton-proton collisions at RHIC. The fully commissioned sPHENIX detector recorded 100 billion unbiased proton-proton collisions in 2024, with more high-statistics data in 2025. The sample enables the first Lambda-c over D-zero baseline at RHIC energies, opening questions on baryon hadronization and strange-to-light flavor ratios.
arxiv-2604-15967: Zhang and nine colleagues expose a flaw in text-to-image models called multi-concept compositional unsafety. Individually safe concepts, combined in one request, can yield harmful or sensitive images, without adversarial prompts, model access, or banned content. They build TwoHamsters to measure the threat: 20k prompts, 51 concept pairs, and six risk categories, tested on 13 models. Prompt-faithful models fail most: FLUX.1 shows a 99.35 percent unsafe alignment rate with a defense rate under 2 percent. Three defenses, filtering, detector tuning, and concept erasure, all fail against unseen combinations.
arxiv-2604-16067: Guransh Singh presents AEGIS, a buffer-free orthogonal gradient projection framework for vision-language fine-tuning. Fine-tuning creates a stability-plasticity dilemma: flow-matching experts send regression gradients into cross-entropy backbones, harming vision. AEGIS measures activation stats from pre-training data as an anchor, then a Wasserstein-2 transport penalty creates an anchor-repair gradient. A backward pass projects updates aside during conflicts. The method sheds only 0.62 percent of energy, halting drift. On LIBERO, it preserves visual question answering and holdout loss while matching action convergence, without buffers.
arxiv-2604-16167: Puglisi, Anand, and Migliaccio train a Cycle-GAN to simulate carbon monoxide emission in the Milky Way, learning from Planck dust maps and HI survey data. They target two CO lines measured by Planck, keeping only sky regions with strong signals, and judge the output by its angular patterns and statistics. The goal is better CO models at high galactic latitudes, where recent surveys have barely looked.
arxiv-2604-16267: Yadav, Woodward, and Forsman improve desalination by grafting polymers onto electrodes. CDI promises efficient water treatment, but suffers weak ion uptake and poor charge use. Their grafted block copolymers boost performance strongly, without changing pore structure. Computer models based on density functional theory and Monte Carlo simulations support the gain. Even simple neutral polymers help, while a designed block architecture helps more.
arxiv-2604-16567: Dufresne and colleagues survey the graph reconstruction conjecture in an overview article. The conjecture claims each graph with three or more vertices is fixed by its deck of vertex-deleted subgraphs. Their invariant approach asks whether polynomials telling apart decks also tell apart original graphs. That move turns a graph problem into an algebraic one. The article surveys the conjecture and its algebraic approach for a broad readership.
arxiv-2604-16867: Chitrao and Ghate compute the reductions modulo a prime p of certain semi-stable representations. Their results cover weights from p plus 5 to 2p and from 2p plus 6 to 3p plus 1, for primes p at least 5. This extends earlier methods beyond the weight range where they previously worked, and sharpens a bound on the valuation of the parameter given by Bergdall, Levin, and Liu.
arxiv-2604-17167: Aronoff and four colleagues assess risks as GENIUS stablecoins scale into mainstream payments and settlement. Redemption at par may hinge not only on backing quality, but on Treasury and repo markets, dealer balance sheets, and blockchain rails. Even soundly backed stablecoins face stress from redemption surges, market bottlenecks, or tech failures. Lasting stability likely needs joined-up market infrastructure, prudential regulation, and software governance.
arxiv-2604-17367: Ye and Zhu prove a Petersen-Wei type volume comparison theorem for weighted Riemannian manifolds, spaces with a notion of curvature twisted by a potential function. The result holds under bounds on the Bakry-Emery Ricci curvature and on the gradient of the potential. As an application, they give a modified proof of a volume comparison and monotonicity result for Kähler-Ricci flow, with an improved error estimate. The work extends comparison geometry to a weighted setting where curvature is controlled only in an averaged sense.
arxiv-2604-17467: Cheng, Peng, Zhang, Zhou, and Pan compare seven dissipation channels in warm Higgs inflation, built from low-temperature, high-temperature, and threshold channels. One unified treatment of background evolution, complexity penalties, and boundary checks maps best-fit points, rankings, and warmness indicators. Except for the pure high-temperature channel, the other six cluster together. The pure low-temperature channel stays top-ranked under a broad scan and a 1,200-point rescoring. Warmness diagnostics place the leader in the strong warm regime.
arxiv-2604-17567: Yang and three colleagues offer tool-free calibration for multi-camera rigs in stick-based sports like golf, baseball, and hockey. Calibrating camera positions is normally costly, yet multi-camera setups are standard for capturing athletes and gear in 3D. Their method jointly uses body keypoints of unknown scale from synced videos and a stick of known length. A three-stage optimization refines camera positions, rebuilds human and stick paths, and fixes scale from the stick length. The paper also releases the first dataset for this task, covering four sports.
arxiv-2604-17667: Ghorbanpour and six colleagues present Peerispect, a hands-on system for claim-level checking in research peer reviews. Reviewers often include claims that are opinion-based, showy, or off-target for the sent-in work, and manual grounding checks cannot scale to modern meetings and journals. Peerispect extracts check-worthy claims from reviews, pulls proof from the paper, and checks claims through natural language logic. Results appear in a visual display flagging proof in the paper, built as a modular search setup for reviewers, authors, and program panels.
arxiv-2604-17767: Yoon shows single-particle interference is set by the phase shared by ready state and detector-defined basis, a value usual interferometers cannot access. With biphoton sources seeded in step, scanning pump, seed, or signal phase gives same sine fringes with contrast near 0.99, a three-scan match absent in two-mode devices. Fringe contrast is tuned through idler overlap, showing quantum which-path info without idler sensing. The bright-dark structure unifies population trapping, EM-induced transparency, discrete photonic patterns, and single-slit diffraction, varying only in dark size.
arxiv-2604-17967: Baaj and Prade establish a precise link between binarized neural networks and Sugeno integrals, which represent input importance and interactions through if-then rules. For a hidden neuron at inference time, they show a hidden neuron's activation threshold test equals a Sugeno integral over binary inputs. That yields an explicit set-function form for each neuron decision and a rule-based representation. They also express the last-layer score as a Sugeno integral, and discuss richer interactions and extensions beyond the binary case.
arxiv-2604-18067: Millar and three colleagues introduce PhysioLite, a lightweight model for ECG and EMG analysis on microcontroller-scale neural processing units. Recent Transformer models perform well but are too large and power-hungry for such hardware, and their dynamic attention clashes with micro-NPU constraints. PhysioLite uses learnable wavelet filters, hardware-aware layer design, and CPU-offloaded positional encoding. It matches Transformer models on ECG and EMG benchmarks at under 10 percent of their size, about 370 kilobytes with 8-bit quantization. Tests on two micro-NPUs confirm viability for wearables.
arxiv-2604-18167: Sambandham and Schön introduce Embedding Arithmetic, a tuning-free way to reduce social bias in text-to-image models at run time. The method adjusts embeddings directly, leaving model weights, prompts, and data sets untouched. A control knob sets the strength of the correction while keeping backgrounds, layouts, and styles intact. Tests on FLUX and Stable Diffusion models show it beats existing baselines on diversity while preserving meaning, judged by a new Concept Coherence Score.
arxiv-2604-18667: Rata presents linear-space data structures for frequency questions on tree paths, including the most common element, the least frequent element, and minority queries. The new structures answer path mode and least-frequent queries faster than the previous best bound, and a randomized method cuts the minority query time further. A general framework for maximum-value color queries on paths covers both the mode and least-frequent cases.
arxiv-2604-19267: Dezons and colleagues propose ViLiNT, a navigation policy for ground robots that blends camera images, 3D laser scans, a goal embedding, and a description of the robot's own body shape. A transformer merges those cues and conditions a diffusion model that draws candidate routes. A clearance head then scores and ranks those routes against the robot's dimensions. The design aims to keep collision avoidance working when environment, robot, or sensors change, and it improves success rates across three simulated settings.
arxiv-2604-19767: Qin, Wan, Mudunuri, and Manoharan benchmark EAGLE3 speculative decoding for PayPal's Commerce Agent, which runs on a fine-tuned llama3.1-nemotron-nano-8B-v1 model. Tests run through vLLM against NVIDIA NIM on identical 2xH100 hardware across 40 configurations. The gamma-3 setting lifts throughput by 22 to 49 percent and cuts latency by 18 to 33 percent at no added hardware cost. Acceptance rates hold steady near 35.5 percent for gamma-3 across all conditions, while gamma-5 gives diminishing returns.
arxiv-2604-19967: Burlak and seven colleagues report a curved microjet and four Herbig-Haro objects near the young star FN Tau, tracing a bipolar outflow dubbed HH 1267. The jet bends rather than running straight, likely because the inner protoplanetary disk precesses, tilting the jet axis under 20 degrees from the line of sight. About 60 years ago the star flared by roughly two magnitudes for several months. The authors link those outbursts to the onset of the microjet.
arxiv-2604-20367: Ji and Luo prove improved lower bounds of Brezin-Li-Yau type for mean sums of Dirichlet eigenvalues for the Laplacian and poly-Laplacian on bounded Euclidean domains. The key step is expanding two binary polynomials that may interest readers on their own. Their bounds improve several existing bounds of this kind in the literature. They are optimal in the sense that the expansions capture all positive terms, whereas earlier work captured only a subset of the positive terms in these two polynomials.
arxiv-2604-20467: Tempest and two colleagues present an open-source tool bringing mechanistic interpretability to AI weather models. These models now rival traditional weather prediction, yet how they reach forecasts is poorly understood. The tool gathers latent representations from the model processor and supports early checks, including cosine similarity and PCA, so users can spot latent directions tied to weather features. Applying it to the graph neural network GraphCast, they show case studies for mid-latitude large-scale waves and specific humidity, finding latent channel mixes matching features a human can read.
arxiv-2604-20567: Savaré studies the rest shape of a thin, elastic, inextensible ribbon, which cuts its bending energy to a minimum. As ribbon width tends to zero, that bending energy tends to the Sadowsky functional. He looks at bent anisotropic ribbons with a possibly curved reference shape. He proves Gamma-convergence still holds under set affine edge rules, including those met by a Möbius strip.
arxiv-2604-20767: Sen, Gangopadhyay, and Vedral study gravity-mediated entanglement of phonons in condensates. They use two slow condensates in traps with same rates, set apart under a gravity model with gravitons as go-between. For low gaps, the entanglement is much higher than that for the mass-entanglement scheme, although its fall is faster than the pair case. When the number of atoms in the cloud is grown, the entanglement for a smaller separation distance becomes higher. That allows for a more robust plan using this phonon protocol.
arxiv-2604-21067: Thomas Schincariol turns conflict deaths into three-dimensional shapes spread over place and time, then matches new outbreaks against past patterns to forecast fatalities. His adapted ShapeFinder method, paired with a distance measure between shapes, beats the established Views ensemble benchmark. The approach gives early-warning work a pattern-matching tool for reading how violence spreads and where it may strike next.
arxiv-2604-21167: Mikhailo Dokuchaev, Emmanuel Jerez, and José Vilca-Rodríguez extend partial group actions to algebras where the grouping of products matters. They solve the problem of building a global version of each partial action inside a chosen variety. Their Lambda-construction gives the needed trait and also covers covariant representations in usual and Lie settings, linking the two sides by an adjoint pair. They further show the construction plays well with semidirect products of Lie algebras.
arxiv-2604-21267: Sodbaatar Adiya and four colleagues find exact invariant solutions for a class of linear time-fractional diffusion-wave equations with variable coefficients, using Lie symmetry analysis. They first pin down the tiny symmetries tied to those coefficients, one by one. Those symmetries then yield solutions in terms of Mittag-Leffler functions, generalized Wright functions, and Fox H-functions. The equations model odd transport and wave motion in many real physical systems, giving the symmetry route a direct payoff in physics.
arxiv-2604-21567: Nusrat Nadia and five others propose an AI system coupling demand forecasting with supply chain optimization for textiles and protective equipment. A Long Short-Term Memory forecasts demand, tracking time patterns, while mixed integer programming sets refills and allocation. It cuts forecasting error and cost. Textile and supply datasets, it beats statistical and deep baselines. Mean absolute error falls from about 15 to about 13 and percentage error from about 10 percent to about 8 percent. Stock cost falls about 5 percent, stockouts 28 percent, and service rises from about 96 percent to about 98 percent.
arxiv-2604-21667: Olufunke Sarumi and colleagues model why annotators disagree, treating each annotator's written reason as a fine-grained signal of that person's view. Their system predicts labels and reasons jointly, using who each annotator is and their profile facts through a User Passport that shapes inner vectors. It offers two explainer designs, one prompt-based and one that links label-model vectors into a text maker. Adding reason modeling beats a simple annotator-aware model on guesses, with the bridge design giving steadier label match.
arxiv-2604-21767: Matos and four colleagues move video misinformation detection from whole-video verdicts to pinpointing the offending span. They transcribe video audio to text and annotate the segments carrying fact-checked false claims, building two datasets with more than 500 videos and over 2,400 annotated segments. Classifiers built on state-of-the-art language models then locate misinformation spans with an F1 score of 0.68 overall. Datasets, transcripts, audio, and videos are released publicly.
arxiv-2604-21967: Romancino studies random entanglement percolation in varied quantum networks, where edge singlet-conversion chances are drawn from a spread rather than fixed. After noting random classical and random quantum entanglement percolation, the paper focuses on polarisation loss as a physical source of random edge entanglement in light networks. In this setting, polarisation imbalance gives a simple map from this loss size to edge singlet-conversion chance. The map is shown for typical loss models, and effects for entanglement percolation are noted.
arxiv-2604-22167: Angell and six colleagues propose a sample-efficient way to estimate harmful-output probabilities for any query. They build unsafe model versions, making harmful outputs more probable through importance sampling. On misuse and misalignment benchmarks, their estimates match Monte Carlo estimates using 10 to 20 times fewer samples. A probability of 10^-4 can be estimated with just 500 samples. Harm scores also reveal input response and predict deployment risks, showing rare-event estimation is critical and feasible for safety evaluations.
arxiv-2604-22267: Bhat and Kumar derive new identities in number theory from summation formulas of Ramanujan and Bailey. They first obtain a few theta function identities at level ten. From those identities they derive a new modular equation of degree five. They then establish Eisenstein series identities, also at level ten. Theta functions and Eisenstein series are both families of functions with rich symmetry properties in number theory.
arxiv-2604-22567: Muirhead and Wigman present strong sign-balance for Laplace eigenfunctions, spurred by small-scale sign patterns. Random eigenfunctions are sign-balanced above one fixed scale, almost always. That scale is best up to a log power of energy. Results cover spherical harmonics and band-limited random waves on Riemannian manifolds. For any level, they fix the best scale above which random eigenfunctions are volume-balanced for non-zero levels. The results also model a guess on the best scale at which deterministic Laplace eigenfunctions are sign-balanced.
arxiv-2604-22867: O'Connor outlines the kinematics of a three-body decay under leading-order changes from a Lorentz-violating quantum field theory. A Dalitz plot, the tool named in the title, maps a three-particle decay onto a plane. It uses pairs of invariant masses, so where events fall inside the allowed region reflects the underlying dynamics. Here the kinematics show how small Lorentz-violating effects reshape the allowed decay region. The paper sets up that analysis for such decays.
arxiv-2604-23067: Padmakumar and three colleagues train a general-purpose red teaming model that extends to arbitrary adversarial goals, including ones it was never directly trained on. Most current automated red teaming targets safety and content moderation, using safety models as evaluators and optimizing to circumvent them. Their pipeline needs no ready-made judge at training time. Fine-tuning small models with it greatly improves attack generation for both in-domain and out-of-domain goals.
arxiv-2604-23267: Ghosh and seven colleagues compare fine-tuning and in-context learning in large language models through formal language tasks with controlled sampling. A discriminative test counts an LLM as proficient when it assigns higher probability to in-language strings than to out-of-language ones. Fine-tuning beats in-context learning on in-distribution generalisation, while both match on out-of-distribution generalisation. Inductive biases look similar at partial learning but diverge at higher proficiency, while in-context learning varies more across models and reacts to token vocabulary.
arxiv-2604-23467: Yadav and Zhao speed up language-model inference by splitting the work between two execution styles: fixed parts replay through CUDA graphs while changing parts run through just-in-time compiled kernels. The hybrid keeps runtime flexibility during token-by-token generation, cutting the wait for the first token by up to about two-thirds against a strong baseline. Tests on a 7-billion-parameter model cover short prompts, where launch overhead matters most.
arxiv-2604-23567: Rahaman, Granot, and Beniamini build a unified analytic framework for synchrotron emission from late-time blast waves once shocks slow into the deep Newtonian regime. There, only a fraction of electrons reach relativistic energies. The transition yields a shallower flux decay for gamma-ray burst afterglows. For kilonova remnants, radio fluxes run several times higher than estimates that ignore the regime. Even non-detections then constrain ambient density and outflow energy.
arxiv-2604-24267: Wang and colleagues describe the GRM pipeline for SVOM's Gamma-Ray Monitor, which detects bursts from 15 keV to 5 MeV. The GRM Instrument Center processes data in real time through X-band, enabling rapid response to high-energy events. An event-driven design handles massive data efficiently with real-time monitoring. Through data production, the system generates L1B and C level products via a task scheduling system, with modular design and automated workflows converting detection data precisely.
arxiv-2604-24467: Zeybek, Mukherjee, and Schmelcher present a gradient-free matrix product state sampling heuristic for discrete quantum optimal control. The matrix product state defines a score function over control parameters, giving a sampling distribution over candidate sequences. The distribution refines step by step by picking better sequences and tuning local tensors to favor the best. Tests on single-qubit state transfer, Bell-pair preparation, qutrit gate implementation, and open-system population transfer show stable convergence. Performance is competitive against established gradient-free baselines.
arxiv-2604-24567: Li, Hong, Tang and Zhong develop a correction adaptive two-grid finite element method for elliptic problems that are nonselfadjoint or indefinite. An earlier adaptive two-grid method required symmetric positive-definite problems. An extra step solves a small residual problem on the coarse mesh at tiny cost, lifting the corrected solution's accuracy. The authors prove convergence through a contraction property and confirm the gains numerically. The method thus widens the reach of two-grid methods to a broader class of problems.
arxiv-2604-25167: Shi and nine colleagues propose Interpretability-Guided Data Selection, a framework that turns interpretability insights into training actions for large language models. It first finds causal task features through frequency recall and interventional filtering. It then selects feature-resonant data that maximally activates those features for fine-tuning. On math, summarization and translation tasks in Gemma-2, LLaMA-3.1 and Qwen3 models, the method beat full-dataset fine-tuning on math by 17.4 percent on Gemma-2-2B while using only half the data. Analysis links stronger feature amplification to better task performance.
arxiv-2604-25467: Zhu and three colleagues propose SSF, a subspace method for federated learning.
